test_title: PYST 38 - SSC CHSL 2025 - English Language (Held On: 26 Nov, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
“Mental health has emerged as a crucial component of an adult’s overall well-being”.

Rewrite the sentence as a negative sentence without changing its meaning.

options.text: Mental health has not failed to emerge as a crucial component of an adult’s overall well-being.
Mental health has not emerged as a crucial component of an adult’s overall well-being.
Mental health doesn’t emerge as a crucial component of an adult’s overall well-being.
Mental health never emerged as a crucial component of an adult’s overall well-being.

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 1: Mental health has not failed to emerge...***

 
 
• To change an affirmative sentence into a negative one without changing its meaning, we often use a **double negative** or an antonym.
 
• The phrase "has not failed to emerge" is logically equivalent to "has emerged." By using "not" + "failed," the sentence becomes grammatically negative while maintaining the original factual statement.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: Mental health has not emerged...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect** because it directly contradicts the original passage. It changes the meaning from "it is a component" to "it is not a component."
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: Mental health doesn’t emerge...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. Similar to Option 2, it changes the meaning to a negative fact. Additionally, it changes the tense from Present Perfect ("has emerged") to Simple Present ("doesn't emerge").
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: Mental health never emerged...***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. It changes the meaning to suggest that the event never happened at all, which is the opposite of the author's intent.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Transformation Rules**: When converting Affirmative to Negative without changing meaning: 

 
 
• Use **Not + Antonym**: (e.g., "He is a good boy" becomes "He is *not a bad* boy").
 
• Use **Double Negatives**: (e.g., "I remember you" becomes "I do *not forget* you").
 
 
 
• **Context**: In the passage, the author highlights mental health as a positive, emerging priority. Option 1 is the only one that upholds this perspective while satisfying the grammatical requirement for a negative word ("not").
